title: Ecobee thermostat has no power or blank screen
shortDescription: Thermostat display is blank or unresponsive due to missing 24V power from the C-wire or PEK.
fullDescription:
Ecobee thermostats require continuous 24VAC power delivered via the C (common) wire or through the Power Extender Kit (PEK) when no C-wire is available. A blank screen typically indicates the thermostat is not receiving the ~24V it needs to operate.

Common root causes include a tripped furnace door safety switch, blown 3A fuse on the HVAC control board, disconnected C-wire, or an incorrectly installed PEK. Some installations use only Rh/Rc/W/Y/G and the unit briefly operates on power stealing before failing.

Resolving this requires verifying HVAC power, checking the low-voltage fuse, and confirming wiring terminations at both the thermostat and the air handler.

causes.cause: Blown 3A fuse on HVAC control board
Incorrectly installed PEK at air handler

fixSteps.title: Check furnace door switch
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure the furnace access panel is fully seated — the safety switch cuts power when open.

fixSteps.title: Inspect 3A fuse
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off HVAC power and check the blade-style 3A fuse on the control board. Replace if blown.

fixSteps.title: Verify C-wire
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm the C-wire is landed on C at both the thermostat base and the control board.

fixSteps.title: Measure voltage
fixSteps.instruction: Measure 24VAC between Rc and C at the thermostat base. If absent, trace back to transformer.

whenToCallPro: Call an HVAC technician if the transformer has failed, voltage is absent at the control board, or wiring is unfamiliar.
videoSearchQuery: Ecobee thermostat blank screen no power fix

faq.q: Can I run Ecobee without a C-wire?
faq.a: Yes — use the included Power Extender Kit (PEK) at the air handler.

faq.q: Why does my Ecobee keep rebooting?
faq.a: Usually insufficient power — install a C-wire or PEK.

title: Ecobee stuck in HVAC Idle and will not call for heat/cool
shortDescription: Thermostat shows HVAC Idle even when setpoint demands heating or cooling.
fullDescription:
The HVAC Idle status indicates Ecobee is not currently calling for any equipment. If it remains idle when there is a legitimate demand, the cause is often a misconfigured equipment profile, a minimum compressor off-time timer, or a Home/Away schedule suppressing activity.

Ecobee enforces a 5-minute compressor protection delay after each cycle. Smart Recovery, Vacation mode, or an extreme outdoor temperature limit on auxiliary heat can also keep the unit idle.

Review Equipment settings, thresholds, and active schedules before concluding the thermostat is faulty.

causes.cause: Incorrect equipment configuration (heat pump vs conventional)

fixSteps.title: Wait compressor delay
fixSteps.instruction: Wait 5-10 minutes for compressor protection delay to clear.

fixSteps.title: Check schedule/mode
fixSteps.instruction: Verify mode is Heat/Cool/Auto and no Vacation event is active.

fixSteps.title: Review equipment settings
fixSteps.instruction: In Installation Settings, confirm equipment type matches your HVAC (heat pump, gas, dual fuel).

whenToCallPro: If equipment configuration is unclear or HVAC still does not respond after correct settings, contact an HVAC pro.
videoSearchQuery: Ecobee HVAC idle not turning on fix

faq.q: Why won't Ecobee turn on my AC?
faq.a: Check compressor delay, mode, and equipment configuration.

title: Ecobee stuck on Calibrating screen
shortDescription: Thermostat shows 'Calibrating' for longer than 20 minutes during initial setup or after reboot.
fullDescription:
Ecobee runs a brief calibration after power cycles to measure room temperature accurately. Normal calibration completes within a few minutes. If the screen shows Calibrating for 20+ minutes, the thermostat is likely stuck because of insufficient power or a firmware glitch.

Power-stealing without a C-wire is the most common cause — the thermostat boots but cannot complete initialization. A factory reset and power verification usually clears the state.

If the problem persists after a C-wire/PEK install, open a ticket with Ecobee support.

fixSteps.title: Wait 20 minutes
fixSteps.instruction: Allow full calibration time before troubleshooting.

fixSteps.title: Pull and reseat thermostat
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the thermostat from its base for 30 seconds, then reattach to trigger a cold boot.

fixSteps.title: Verify C-wire/PEK
fixSteps.instruction: Install a C-wire or Power Extender Kit if not already present.

whenToCallPro: If calibration persists after a proven C-wire connection, contact Ecobee support for warranty replacement.

faq.a: Usually 2-5 minutes. Over 20 minutes indicates a problem.

title: Ecobee reports Equipment Not Running alert
shortDescription: Thermostat detects it is calling for heat/cool but temperature is not changing as expected.
fullDescription:
Ecobee monitors whether the indoor temperature responds when equipment is called. If temperature does not move within an expected window, it raises an Equipment Not Running alert via the app.

This usually points to a real HVAC issue: tripped breaker, low refrigerant, clogged filter, condensate overflow float switch, or frozen evaporator coil. It can also be a false alarm during mild weather or when a door/window is open.

Inspect the HVAC equipment directly before assuming a thermostat problem.

causes.cause: Tripped HVAC breaker or furnace switch

fixSteps.title: Check breaker
fixSteps.instruction: Reset the HVAC breaker and furnace switch.

fixSteps.title: Replace filter
fixSteps.instruction: Install a clean air filter; let any frozen coil thaw for 4 hours.

fixSteps.title: Empty condensate line
fixSteps.instruction: Clear clogged condensate drain; reset float switch.

whenToCallPro: Refrigerant issues, compressor failures, and repeated condensate overflow require an HVAC professional.
videoSearchQuery: Ecobee equipment not running alert fix

faq.a: Yes, but verify the HVAC is actually working first.

title: Ecobee lost Wi-Fi connection
shortDescription: Thermostat shows a disconnected Wi-Fi icon and cannot reach the Ecobee cloud.
fullDescription:
Ecobee thermostats use 2.4GHz Wi-Fi for cloud connectivity. A Wi-Fi drop prevents remote control, schedules continue to run locally using the last-synced program. Common causes include router reboots, SSID or password changes, 5GHz-only networks, or weak signal at the thermostat location.

If multiple devices dropped at once, the issue is usually the router. If only Ecobee is affected, re-enter credentials from the thermostat's Wi-Fi settings menu.

Ecobee does not support captive portals (hotel Wi-Fi) or WPA3-only networks.

fixSteps.title: Restart router
fixSteps.instruction: Power cycle your router and wait 2 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Reconnect Wi-Fi
fixSteps.instruction: On thermostat: Settings > Wi-Fi > select network > enter password.

fixSteps.title: Switch security mode
fixSteps.instruction: Set router to WPA2 or WPA2/WPA3 mixed mode.

whenToCallPro: If Wi-Fi cannot be re-established after router and credential checks, contact Ecobee support.

title: Ecobee SmartSensor will not pair or drops offline
shortDescription: Room sensor fails to pair with thermostat or repeatedly shows as offline.
fullDescription:
Ecobee SmartSensors use a proprietary 915MHz mesh and pair via the thermostat's Sensors menu. Pairing issues are usually caused by a dead coin cell, the tab still present in new sensors, or distance beyond ~45 ft from the thermostat.

Sensors that pair and then drop offline generally need a fresh CR2032 battery. Metal shelves, refrigerators, and concrete walls can also block signal.

Remove and re-add the sensor from the thermostat if it remains stuck in an unpaired state.

fixSteps.title: Pull tab or replace battery
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the plastic pull-tab or install a fresh CR2032.

fixSteps.title: Re-pair sensor
fixSteps.instruction: On thermostat: Main Menu > Sensors > Add Sensor; place sensor within 3 ft during pairing.

fixSteps.title: Relocate sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Move sensor closer to thermostat or remove metallic obstructions.

whenToCallPro: Rarely required. Contact Ecobee support if a new sensor fails to pair with a fresh battery.
videoSearchQuery: Ecobee smart sensor not pairing fix

faq.q: How many sensors can I pair?
faq.a: Up to 32 on a Premium/Enhanced, 32 on SmartThermostat.

title: Ecobee temperature reading is inaccurate
shortDescription: Displayed room temperature differs from reality by several degrees.
fullDescription:
Ecobee includes a built-in temperature sensor plus any paired SmartSensors. Inaccuracy is typically caused by the thermostat being mounted on an exterior wall, near a heat source, in direct sunlight, or with air leaking from the wall behind it.

Ecobee provides a Temperature Correction setting (-9 to +9 F) under Installation Settings > Thresholds. This should be used only after confirming the physical environment is appropriate.

If SmartSensors report inaccurate values, replace the CR2032 and confirm the sensor isn't in sun or near electronics.

causes.cause: Thermostat in sunlight or near heat source
Air leak from wall behind thermostat

fixSteps.title: Check mounting location
fixSteps.instruction: Move away from sunlight, lamps, TVs, or vents.

fixSteps.title: Seal wall opening
fixSteps.instruction: Stuff insulation into the low-voltage hole behind the thermostat base.

fixSteps.title: Apply correction
fixSteps.instruction: Main Menu > Settings > Installation Settings > Thresholds > Temperature Correction.

whenToCallPro: If offset of more than 5°F is needed after sealing the wall, request warranty service.

title: Ecobee humidity reading missing or stuck
shortDescription: Thermostat reports implausible humidity (0%, 100%) or no reading.
fullDescription:
Ecobee's internal humidity sensor can drift after long exposure to high humidity or dust. Readings of 0% or 100% generally mean the sensor has saturated or the ADC has failed.

Soft remedies include a thermostat reboot, firmware update, and applying a humidity correction under Installation Settings. Persistent 0/100% values usually require warranty replacement because the sensor is soldered to the main board.

Humidifier/dehumidifier output can still run if you configure humidity control with a SmartSensor or external source.

causes.cause: Sensor saturated after long high humidity

fixSteps.title: Reboot thermostat
fixSteps.instruction: Pull from base for 30s and reattach.

fixSteps.title: Update firmware
fixSteps.instruction: Main Menu > About > Check for Update.

fixSteps.title: Contact warranty
fixSteps.instruction: If reading persists, file a claim with Ecobee (3-5 year warranty).

whenToCallPro: Humidity IC failures require Ecobee warranty replacement.

faq.a: No — it's soldered to the main board; request a replacement unit.

title: Ecobee Premium air quality monitor not reporting
shortDescription: VOC, CO2, or PM sensor reads error or provides no data (Ecobee Premium only).
fullDescription:
Ecobee Premium ships with an indoor air quality (IAQ) monitor that tracks VOC, CO2-eq, and particulate matter. The sensor requires a 24-hour burn-in period after install. If after 24h it still shows no data or an error, confirm firmware is current and reboot.

Cleaning products, new paint, or nearby stoves can saturate the VOC sensor for hours. This is normal and readings recover once the air clears.

Hardware failure of the IAQ module requires warranty service.

fixSteps.title: Ventilate room
fixSteps.instruction: Open windows 30 min to flush VOC saturation.

fixSteps.title: Update + reboot
fixSteps.instruction: Install latest firmware and pull/reseat thermostat.

whenToCallPro: Persistent errors after burn-in and firmware update need Ecobee warranty.

title: Ecobee firmware update fails or hangs
shortDescription: Thermostat cannot complete an OTA firmware update.
fullDescription:
Ecobee pushes firmware updates automatically during overnight windows. Failures generally trace to Wi-Fi instability, limited power, or server-side issues at Ecobee.

Let the thermostat retry for 24 hours — most failures resolve without action. If it's still stuck, force an update from Main Menu > About > Check for Update, then reboot.

Thermostats on power-stealing without a C-wire sometimes cannot hold connection long enough to complete the download.

fixSteps.title: Let it retry overnight
fixSteps.instruction: Ecobee automatically re-attempts updates in low-use hours.

fixSteps.title: Force update
fixSteps.instruction: Main Menu > About > Check for Update.

fixSteps.title: Check Ecobee status
fixSteps.instruction: Visit status.ecobee.com to confirm no outage.

whenToCallPro: If bricked by a failed update, contact Ecobee support.

title: Ecobee heat pump blowing cold in heat mode
shortDescription: Reversing valve O/B polarity configured incorrectly for the heat pump.
fullDescription:
Heat pumps use an O or B reversing valve signal to select heating or cooling. If configured wrong, cooling runs when you call for heat and vice-versa. Most modern heat pumps use O (energize on cool); older Rheem/Ruud systems use B (energize on heat).

Change this in Installation Settings > Equipment > Reversing Valve. Do not change wiring — only the thermostat setting.

Wrong configuration does not damage equipment but will never satisfy setpoint.

causes.cause: O vs B set incorrectly in Installation Settings

fixSteps.title: Open Equipment Settings
fixSteps.instruction: Main Menu > Settings > Installation Settings > Equipment > Heat Pump > Reversing Valve.

fixSteps.title: Toggle O/B
fixSteps.instruction: Switch between O (energize on cool) and B (energize on heat).

fixSteps.title: Test cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Call for heat, confirm warm supply air; then call for cool.

whenToCallPro: Only if unsure which type your system uses — consult HVAC installer.
videoSearchQuery: Ecobee heat pump reversing valve O B fix

faq.a: O — used by most modern heat pumps.

title: Ecobee runs auxiliary heat too often
shortDescription: Aux/strip heat is activating in conditions that should allow the heat pump alone.
fullDescription:
Ecobee calls auxiliary heat when the heat pump cannot meet demand. Excessive aux use drives up electric bills. Common triggers: aggressive setpoint recovery, incorrect compressor-to-aux differential, low outdoor temperature balance point, or actual heat pump underperformance.

Review Smart Recovery behavior and adjust 'Compressor to Aux Temp Delta' under Thresholds. For dual-fuel setups, confirm balance point temperature matches your climate.

Persistent aux use with correct settings indicates a refrigerant or defrost issue.

fixSteps.title: Increase aux delta
fixSteps.instruction: Set 'Compressor to Aux Temp Delta' to 2-3°F.

fixSteps.title: Disable smart recovery
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off Smart Recovery to prevent preheating spikes.

fixSteps.title: Set outdoor temp sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Link weather station and set lockouts for aux heat.

whenToCallPro: If aux stays on with correct thresholds, have HVAC check refrigerant and defrost.
videoSearchQuery: Ecobee auxiliary heat running too much fix

faq.a: No, but excessive use is costly.
